To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the antisense reduction of NADP malic enzyme (ME) activity in the C4 plant Flaveria bidents reduces CO2 leakiness and that antisense reduction of the Rubisco small subunits increases CO2 leakiness.

the C4 cycle in the dicot Fl. bidentis can be reduced in vivo by 34% to >75% without a visible phenotype and that this reduction in C4 activity results in a lower leakiness of CO 2 from the bundle sheaths.

(1) the antisense reduction of NADP malic enzyme in F. bident is plants reduced the rate of CO 2 flow through the C 4 cycle and (2) this reduction in CO 2 flow was associated with a reduction in the rate of C 4 decarboxylation and an increase in the rate of Rubisco carboxylation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the C4 pathway functions in vivo and the extent to which it can be manipulated.
how plants use the C4 cycle to optimize photosynthesis and how this cycle is regulated.
the regulation of the C4 cycle and how it is coordinated with the C3 cycle to optimize photosynthesis.

The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to alter the C4 cycle through genetic manipulation.

transgenic manipulation of C4 plants provides an opportunity to dissect the complex interactions of C3 and C3 photosynthesis and to understand the mechanisms of CO2 fixation that have evolved in the C4 pathway.
